title: Generalized Weakness
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with episodes of confusion, diaphoresis, tremors, palpitations, and generalized weakness — relieved by eating (Whipple's triad: hypoglycemic symptoms + low glucose <50 mg/dL + relief with glucose administration). Insulinoma is a neuroendocrine tumor of pancreatic beta cells causing inappropriate insulin secretion → fasting hypoglycemia. Diagnosis: supervised 72-hour fast — will develop hypoglycemia with inappropriately elevated insulin + C-peptide levels (endogenous insulin). Insulin:glucose ratio elevated. Sulfonylurea screen negative (rules out factitious hypoglycemia). Localization: CT/MRI abdomen, endoscopic ultrasound, or selective arterial calcium stimulation. Treatment: surgical resection (enucleation). If unresectable or metastatic: diazoxide (suppresses insulin secretion), octreotide, everolimus. Frequent small meals, avoid prolonged fasting.
chief_complaint: Episodic confusion, sweating, weakness relieved by eating
